subject: community-medicine
title: Energy Requirements: ICMR Reference Man and Balanced Diets

steps.title: The revised ICMR reference man standards
steps.tx: To establish baseline nutritional and energy standards, the Indian Council of Medical Research defines the **ICMR reference man**, updated to reflect contemporary Indian anthropometry. He is an Indian adult male aged nineteen to thirty-nine years, weighing sixty-five kilograms, standing one point seven seven metres tall (height 177 cm), with a normal body mass index of twenty point seven, free from disease, engaged in eight hours of occupational work.
steps.say: The ICMR reference man is between nineteen and thirty-nine years old, weighs sixty-five kilograms, stands one hundred and seventy-seven centimetres tall, and works an eight-hour shift daily.

steps.title: The ICMR reference woman standards
steps.tx: Complementing the male standard, the updated **ICMR reference woman** is defined as an Indian adult female between nineteen and thirty-nine years of age, weighing fifty-five kilograms, standing one point six two metres tall (height 162 cm), with a normal body mass index of twenty-one point zero. When calculating nutritional needs, pregnancy demands an extra three hundred and fifty kilocalories daily, while lactation requires an additional six hundred kilocalories.
steps.say: The ICMR reference woman weighs fifty-five kilograms and stands one hundred and sixty-two centimetres tall. Pregnancy requires an extra three hundred and fifty calories every day.

steps.title: Physical activity levels: sedentary, moderate, heavy
steps.tx: Energy expenditure varies fundamentally with occupational exertion, categorized into three standardized tiers: sedentary, moderate and heavy work. A sedentary man requires approximately two thousand one hundred and ten kilocalories daily, moderate work (agriculturalists, domestic chores) requires two thousand seven hundred and ten kilocalories, while heavy manual labour (stone cutters, rickshaw pullers, blacksmiths) demands three thousand four hundred and seventy kilocalories to meet **occupational energy requirement**.
steps.say: Daily calorie needs depend on occupational exertion. A sedentary man requires about two thousand one hundred calories, moderate work needs two thousand seven hundred, and heavy manual labor needs three thousand five hundred.

steps.title: Components of total energy expenditure
steps.tx: Daily caloric expenditure comprises three distinct physiological components: basal metabolic rate, diet-induced thermogenesis, and the energy cost of physical activity. The **basal metabolic rate** accounts for sixty to seventy percent of total daily energy expenditure, representing the obligatory energy expended to maintain cellular respiration, autonomic cardiac contraction, renal filtration and ionic membrane gradients in a thermal neutral resting state.
steps.say: Basal metabolic rate accounts for nearly two-thirds of your daily calories, powering breathing, brain activity, heartbeat and body temperature even while you sleep.

steps.title: The concept of a balanced diet
steps.tx: A scientifically constructed **balanced diet framework** supplies all required macronutrients and micronutrients in proper quantities and exact proportions to sustain optimal physiological function, support physical growth, maintain cellular repair, and provide a small buffer reserve for brief periods of starvation or acute illness. No single foodstuff is nutritionally complete on its own, demanding diverse combinations across all five essential food groups.
steps.say: A balanced diet provides all nutrients in the right proportions to maintain health, repair tissues, and provide a safety reserve during illness, drawn across all food groups.

rows: Plant protein, iron, folate, soluble fibre

steps.tx: The plate sets vegetables, pulses, grains, and dairy side by side because no single food covers every need. A **balanced diet framework** supplies macronutrients and micronutrients in the amounts and proportions that support function, growth, and cellular repair, and it leaves a small reserve for short starvation or acute illness. Diversity across all five essential food groups is required. Completeness belongs to the whole plate, not to any one portion on it.
steps.say: No single food contains every nutrient in the right amount. A balanced plate draws on all five food groups so the body can grow, repair cells, and keep a small reserve for short illness or missed meals.

steps.title: The five food groups and plate model
steps.tx: To translate complex nutrient numbers into practical kitchen plates, the National Institute of Nutrition promotes the **My Plate for the Day** visual model. Recommending a total daily food mass of two kilograms (including water), the circular plate dictates that half the plate should consist of vegetables, green leafy vegetables and fresh fruits, one quarter should be cereals and millets, and the remaining quarter shared between pulses and dairy.
steps.say: The national plate model dictates that half your plate should be vegetables and fresh fruits, one quarter whole grains and millets, and one quarter protein-rich pulses and dairy.

steps.title: Protein requirement standards in grams per kilogram
steps.tx: The updated Indian nutritional guidelines establish an **adult protein requirement** of zero point eight three grams of good quality protein per kilogram body weight per day (rounded to approximately fifty-four grams for the reference man and forty-six grams for the reference woman). Meeting this target through plant-based diets demands selecting combinations that provide diverse amino acids, avoiding exclusive reliance on a single polished cereal.
steps.say: Healthy adults need zero point eight three grams of protein per kilogram body weight daily, totaling about fifty-four grams for men and forty-six grams for women.

steps.tx: Egg beside lentils on a school tray shows how mixed foods meet a protein target that one cereal cannot. Guidelines set an **adult protein requirement** of 0.83 grams of good quality protein per kilogram of body weight each day, about 54 grams for the reference man and 46 grams for the reference woman. Plant meals have to bring different amino acids together. A plate built only on one polished cereal misses that target even when it looks full.
steps.say: Adults need about 0.83 grams of good quality protein per kilogram each day, near 54 grams for men and 46 grams for women. Egg with lentils supplies a wider set of amino acids than a meal of one polished cereal.

steps.title: Dietary diversity score and micronutrient adequacy
steps.tx: At the household level, community health officers measure diet quality using the **dietary diversity score**, which tallies the number of distinct food groups consumed over the preceding twenty-four hours. Consuming items from at least five out of ten standardized food groups correlates robustly with micronutrient adequacy, protecting mothers and young children against hidden hunger, iron deficiency anaemia, and subclinical zinc deficits.
steps.say: The dietary diversity score counts how many food groups a family ate over the past day. Eating from five or more groups guarantees adequate vitamins and minerals.

steps.title: Nutrition transition and the double burden of malnutrition
steps.tx: Developing economies in South Asia face the perilous **double burden of malnutrition**, characterized by the simultaneous coexistence of childhood undernutrition, stunting and wasting alongside adult overweight, central adiposity, type 2 diabetes and hypertension within the same communities or households. This nutrition transition stems from easy availability of cheap ultra-processed refined foods combined with declining occupational physical activity, demanding integrated policy responses.
steps.say: The double burden of malnutrition means families suffer from child stunting and adult diabetes at the same time. Cheap processed snacks replace nutritious foods, fueling the chronic disease crisis.
